title: Coordinates over a specified coefficient field in a complete regular local ring
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $(C,\mathfrak p)$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian regular local ring of finite Krull dimension $d$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], complete for $\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], and let $c:k\to C$ be a ring map inducing an isomorphism $k\xrightarrow{\sim}C/\mathfrak p$. For every $t_1,\ldots,t_d\in\mathfrak p$ generating $\mathfrak p$, the continuous $k$-algebra homomorphism $k[[T_1,\ldots,T_d]]\to C$, with coefficients mapped by $c$ and $T_i\mapsto t_i$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], is an isomorphism of complete local $k$-algebras. For $d=0$ the list is empty and this says that $c:k\to C$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0C0S (lemma-regular-complete-containing-coefficient-field), clause (2) and its proof, choosing any basis of the cotangent space; lines 45036–45066.

proof.text: For every d, including d = 0, form P = k[[T_1,...,T_d]]. The field branch of [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete] gives a local domain of dimension d, complete for its maximal ideal I, and identifies I with the variables ideal. The Cohen-ring branch is impossible since k is a field. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-universal-property-complete] to c and t to obtain f with f(C(a)) = c(a) and f(X_i) = t_i.

Mapping the span of the variables by f gives the span of t, hence I.map f = maximalIdeal C. Every residue class is the residue of some c(a) by hres, hence is the image of the constant series C(a). The target is Hausdorff for I.map f, since this is its maximal ideal. The source is precomplete for I. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complete-source-surjective-mod-ideal] to obtain surjectivity of f.

If a nonzero x lies in ker f, the domain property of P makes x a nonzerodivisor. Apply [lem-trf-surjective-kernel-nonzerodivisor-dimension-drop] directly to f. It gives dim C + 1 <= dim P. Both dimensions equal the finite integer d, so this contradicts d + 1 <= d. Therefore f is injective. No calculation of the constant coefficient of x, or exact dimension formula for a principal quotient, is needed.

Form e = RingEquiv.ofBijective f. Its coefficient and variable equations are those of f. Ideal.map_pow and I.map f = maximalIdeal C give (I^r).map f = (maximalIdeal C)^r for every natural r, including zero. Ideal.comap_map_of_bijective gives the required comap equality.

When d = 0, MvPowerSeries.isEmptyEquiv says every F equals C(constantCoeff F). Surjectivity of f therefore implies surjectivity of c, since f agrees with c on constants. A unital map from the field k to the nontrivial local ring C is injective, so c is bijective.

tool_uses.why: Generic algebraic input: power series over a field are Noetherian local domains, complete, with residue field k and dimension d; this unit has no replacement for these ring facts.
Generic complete-ring evaluation of a multivariate series at elements of the ideal of completeness, with its truncation formula; no trace-formula-specific construction replaces it.
Generic successive-approximation criterion for surjectivity of a ring map from a complete source; used exactly as Stacks 0C0S invokes 0315.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q74-cbcff67a6 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and all six cited statements in full, and Stacks algebra.tex Tag 0C0S(2) and its proof at lines 45036-45066 (it uses 0315 and 00KW). The statement matches clause (2): it fixes the coefficient map c and takes any d generators of p, which for dim C = d are exactly a basis of p/p^2. The citer lem-trf-relative-cohen-flat-presentation uses the item with exactly this specified-coefficient form. Step 1 (d=0): the empty list generates p, so p=0 and C=k via c; the zero-variable series ring is k by the definition node. Step 2: the universal-property node is applied with a=p and alpha=c; its truncation formula gives psi(I^r) inside p^r, so psi is continuous. Step 3: IC=p, the constants make P->C/p onto, P is I-complete by clause (3) of the Cohen-regular node, and C is p-Hausdorff; these are exactly the hypotheses of the 0315 Mathlib leaf. Step 4: a nonzero f in the kernel has f(0)=0 because k->C/p is injective, so f lies in I and is a nonzerodivisor (P is a domain). The 00KW leaf then gives dim P/fP = d-1, while C is a quotient of P/fP, so d <= d-1, a contradiction. Step 5: psi(I^r)=p^r and bijectivity give psi^-1(p^r)=I^r, so the inverse is continuous. Edge cases: C=k; C=k[[U]] with T->uU for a unit u; and C=k[[U,V]]/(UV), which the hypotheses exclude (dim 1 but two generators needed). Imperfect or characteristic-p k is harmless because c is given. Duplicates: lem-per-prime-field-complete-coordinate-model is existence-only and on the route-pivot dropped list, the pbc full-coordinates and parameter-quotient nodes assume the target is already a power-series ring, and no node states the item. Route: neither the item, its citer, its via ancestors nor its deps are in route-pivot-dropped.txt; there is no repair note and no SGA source. I accept the three generic pbc algebra tool_uses. No new nodes and no fixes.

lean.statement: theorem exists_ringEquiv_regular_complete_coefficients (k : Type u) [Field k] (C : Type v) [CommRing C] [IsRegularLocalRing C] [IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal C) C] (d : ℕ) (hdim : ringKrullDim C = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) (c : k →+* C) (hres : Function.Bijective ((residue C).comp c)) (t : Fin d → C) (ht : ∀ i : Fin d, t i ∈ maximalIdeal C) (hgen : Ideal.span (Set.range t) = maximalIdeal C) : (∃ e : MvPowerSeries (Fin d) k ≃+* C, (∀ a : k, e (MvPowerSeries.C a) = c a) ∧ (∀ i : Fin d, e (MvPowerSeries.X i) = t i) ∧ (∀ r : ℕ, Ideal.comap e.toRingHom (maximalIdeal C ^ r) = Ideal.span (Set.range (MvPowerSeries.X : Fin d → MvPowerSeries (Fin d) k)) ^ r)) ∧ (d = 0 → Function.Bijective c)
